title: Enterprise Onboarding: Integrations, Escalations, Known Issues, Health Checks & QBR Playbook
author: Jordan Patel
content:
Overview:

This playbook consolidates enterprise onboarding guidance for integrations, escalation paths, known issues and workarounds, ongoing support process, and quarterly business review (QBR) / health-check materials. It is intended for Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Solutions Engineers (SEs), Support Engineers, and on-call SREs who participate in enterprise onboarding and ongoing account health.

Sections included:
- Onboarding phases and owner matrix
- Integration checklist and reference guides
- Escalation playbook (tiering, SLAs, routing, and templates)
- Known issues and workarounds (most common enterprise items)
- Ongoing support process and SLAs / SLOs
- Health checks and QBR templates + sample agendas

Audience and scope:
- Audience: CSMs, SEs, Support, SREs, Account Execs.
- Scope: Applies to all enterprise customers onboarding Redwood Private, Dedicated, or Hosted API with enterprise support contracts. For smaller self-serve customers, use the condensed Quick Onboarding checklist.

1) Onboarding phases and owner matrix

Phases:
1. Discovery & Contracting (Pre-sales / AM)
2. Kickoff & Technical Readiness (CSM + SE)
3. Integration & Validation (SE + Customer Eng)
4. Performance & Scale Run (SRE + Eng)
5. Production Cutover & Handover (CSM + Support)
6. Ongoing Operations & QBRs (CSM + Support + SRE as needed)

Owner matrix (high level):
- CSM: project management, customer communications, QBRs
- SE: integration guidance, API keys, SDK guidance, prompt engineering suggestions
- Support Engineer: triage for incidents, provide known-workaround guidance, escalate to SRE/Eng
- SRE/Platform Eng: capacity planning, incident response, performance tuning; owner for runbook updates

2) Integration checklist and reference guides

Integration checklist (minimum required items before validation):
- [ ] Signed contract and support level verified
- [ ] Customer account and billing setup complete
- [ ] API keys exchanged and stored in vault (recommend KMS/HSM)
- [ ] Network connectivity validated (VPC peering / firewall rules)
- [ ] Model selection and baseline configuration documented (model id + quantization profile)
- [ ] Test prompts and validation dataset agreed (10-50 representative prompts)
- [ ] Latency & throughput targets defined (p50/p95/p99 expectations)
- [ ] Logging and audit collection configured (log destination + retention)
- [ ] Rollout plan and rollback criteria agreed (canary %, duration, health gates)

Common CLI / API commands to validate connectivity:
- curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate" -d '{"model":"redwood-large-v1","prompt":"hello"}'
- kubectl get pods -n redwood-customer-123 (for private deployments)

Integration best practices:
- Use per-environment keys (dev/staging/prod) and rotate keys at cutover
- Start with a conservative concurrency and increase by 30% per day while monitoring latency and error rates
- Enable prefix caching for batched endpoints where appropriate

3) Escalation playbook

Severity definitions and target response times (enterprise SLA):
- Sev 1 (Critical): Platform down or customer production outage impacting >50% users — initial response within 15 minutes, continuous updates every 30 minutes, target full remediation based on incident runbook
- Sev 2 (High): Degraded performance causing severe user impact (high latency/errors) — initial response within 1 hour, updates every 2 hours
- Sev 3 (Medium): Functional but with reduced quality or intermittent issues — acknowledge within 4 business hours, resolution in next 72 hours
- Sev 4 (Low): Minor bug or documentation request — respond within 2 business days

Escalation routing steps:
1. Support queue triage (Support Engineers) — gather logs, request customer context (timestamps, request ids, sample payloads)
2. If not resolvable within 60 minutes for Sev 1 or 4 hours for Sev 2, escalate to SRE on-call and assign incident channel (#inc-<customer>-<yyyyMMdd>)
3. SRE performs triage; if root cause requires product engineering, SRE creates a P0/P1 ticket and notifies Eng on-call and relevant owners
4. Notify CSM and AM about customer impact and planned communications cadence
5. Post-incident: complete postmortem within 3 business days for Sev 1/2 incidents; share with customer and internal stakeholders

Communication templates (first notification):
Subject: [Redwood] Incident Report — {customer} — {Short summary}
Body:
- Impact: {services affected, customer impact estimate}
- Time detected: {UTC timestamp}
- Status: Investigating / Mitigating / Resolved
- Next update: {ETA}
- Contact: {Support escalation lead contact}

4) Known issues and workarounds (top enterprise items)

Issue: Intermittent 503 errors during heavy batching
Workaround: Reduce concurrency per client, enable smaller batch sizes, and temporarily pin to a lower-latency model variant. SRE action: investigate kernel saturation and increase worker count for model-serving pool.

Issue: VPC peering fails due to asymmetric routing
Workaround: Validate route tables and NAT gateway configuration; recommend customer enable full mesh routes or use a dedicated transit gateway. Provide example AWS route table JSON for reference.

Issue: Tokenization mismatch causing output truncation on multilingual prompts
Workaround: Use model-specific tokenizers in SDK (example: python snippet to set tokenizer utf-8 handling) and add pre-processing hook to normalize input.

Issue: Billing spikes from unexpected high-rate synthetic traffic
Workaround: Temporarily add rate-limiting at API gateway and enable quota enforcement per API key. Provide CSM with daily cost delta report and recommend usage caps.

Known-issue triage checklist:
1. Reproduce with customer sample request (obtain PII-safe sample)
2. Collect request_id, timestamps, and server pod logs
3. Check model-serving metrics (cpu/gpu utilization, queue length) and cache hit ratios
4. Apply documented workaround and monitor customer impact
5. If recurring, add to regression-triage board and schedule a fix with Eng

5) Support process, SLAs, and handoffs

Support intake channels:
- Enterprise support portal (preferred) — creates ticket automatically into Zendesk with metadata tags
- Email to enterprise-support@redwood.example — creates ticket; allow response SLA
- Priority phone line for Sev 1 customers

Ticket lifecycle and ownership:
- Initial triage by Support (Triage within SLA window above)
- Assign to SE or SRE based on problem type (integration/config vs runtime/infra)
- For engineering bugs, create a tracking JIRA and link to support ticket; update customer weekly until fix is shipped

Handover to Customer Success:
- After production cutover, schedule 30/60/90 day check-ins (automated calendar invites with owner = CSM)
- Provide transfer document with: integration checklist status, outstanding tickets, usage dashboard link, and recommended next steps

Metrics we track for enterprise health:
- MTTR by severity (target MTTR: Sev1 < 4 hours median, Sev2 < 24 hours median)
- Time to first response (enterprise SLA targets above)
- Number of open high-severity issues per customer (target 0)
- Monthly usage trend vs. baseline (identify anomalies)

6) Health checks and QBR materials

Quarterly health-check items (CSM checklist):
- Usage summary: tokens, embeddings calls, peak qps, and average latency (p50/p95)
- Cost summary: monthly spend vs committed/forecasted usage
- Reliability summary: uptime, incidents since last QBR, outstanding tickets
- Performance tuning suggestions: batching, cache settings, suggested model/quantization adjustments
- Security and compliance: audit log health, rotation of keys, retention policy review

QBR template (60 minutes):
- 0-5 min: Introductions and agenda
- 5-15 min: Business goals and success metrics review (customer)
- 15-30 min: Usage & performance review (CSM)
- 30-40 min: Incidents / Reliability review and action items (Support/SRE)
- 40-50 min: Roadmap & upcoming features that impact the customer (Product/Eng)
- 50-60 min: Action items, owners, and next steps (CSM)

Pre-QBR deliverables (CSM):
- Distribute QBR deck 3 business days prior
- Provide support summary and link to incident postmortems since last QBR
- Share optimization recommendations and expected cost/latency impact

Post-QBR follow-up:
- Create action tracker with owners and due dates (linked in CRM)
- If any technical action requires engineering work, create a scoped ticket and mark priority level

Appendices

A. Sample QBR slide bullet points (copyable):
- Key wins since last QBR: successful cutover to Dedicated pool, restored p95 latency to 260ms
- Current risks: 2 high-priority tickets open related to VPC networking
- Recommendations: enable prefix caching + adjust batch size from 32 to 16 for chat endpoint

B. Contact list and escalation contacts:
- Enterprise Support (primary): enterprise-support@redwood.example
- Sev 1 Pager: +1-800-REDCALL (for urgent customer incidents)
- On-call SRE channel: #sre-oncall
- CSM escalation lead: csm-leads@redwood.example

C. Runbook links and artifacts (internal):
- /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/incident-management
- /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/release-notes
- /confluence/customer-success-and-support/enterprise-onboarding-support-playbook-2026-03-15

D. Change log (summary of major updates):
- 2025-11-15: Initial draft and rollout to CSM org
- 2026-01-10: Added explicit Sev definitions and SLA windows per enterprise contract
- 2026-03-04: Updated known issues section with new batching 503 mitigation and added QBR template

If you are a CSM or SE preparing for an onboarding kickoff, use the "Onboarding Kickoff Checklist" task template and attach this playbook. For any gaps in this playbook or if a customer requires a tailor-made onboarding plan, please reach out to the customer-success playbook owners (see reviewers) and request a 1:1 review.
